claims.text: Threshold matter for the record: the three artifacts describe the same trip. The trip_id TRP-00109 appears on the trip record, the GPS trace and the fare breakdown, and the trace's first fix (2026-07-21T18:21:10) matches the trip record's started_at to the second, so the rider's initial burden under limb (a) is discharged on matching identifiers and a matching pickup timestamp.

On the governing trace field the trip covers 13.76 km against a booked optimal of 6.4 km - an excess of 7.36 km, which is 115% of the optimal route. Both POL-RD-01 gates are cleared (more than 0.8 km absolute, more than 20% relative), and because the excess also exceeds 50% of optimal the deviation is additionally MATERIAL, exactly as the trace-derived status records. The rider's limb (b) burden is discharged.

POL-RD-01 makes gps_trace.trace_distance_km the governing measurement and expressly forbids citing trip_record.actual_distance_km for the threshold test. The rider measures on the trace's 13.76 km, and that figure clears the gate by itself, so nothing in this case turns on the rounded 13.8 km convenience copy on the trip record.

The traffic-advisory artifact is MISSING: no advisory covers this corridor on this trip, and absence is citable. I disclose that EV-ADVIS-00109-01 carries weight 0.0, has no payload, and fired the issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT. With no named road or expressway segment, no validity window overlapping the trace, and no matched corridor exit and rejoin, POL-RD-03 exonerates nothing here - the driver has no road-condition answer to the deviation.

Neither of the other baseline-lifting clauses is available to the driver. pickup_amended_at and dropoff_amended_at are both null and amended_optimal_distance_km is null, so there is no re-quote for POL-RD-05 to re-run POL-RD-01 against; and vehicle_type is RYDE_X, not RYDE_POOL, so the matched-itinerary baseline of POL-RD-12 never arises. The comparison stays where the rider put it: 13.76 km driven against 6.4 km optimal.

The rider's own message at 18:22:06 asked for a stop - 'stop at jurong point first? need to grab something 5 min'. POL-RD-04 excuses a deviation only 'to the extent' it is attributable to such an instruction: it excludes the excess distance between leaving and rejoining the optimal corridor and nothing beyond that. It does not reclassify the whole 7.36 km excess as a lawful trip, it does not displace POL-RD-01 or POL-RD-02 for any excess left over from the subtraction, and the size of the attributable portion is the driver's to establish under POL-RD-08. The record carries no derived measurement of that portion at all, so the exclusion cannot be shown to consume the rider's whole excess.

The fare model is METERED and quoted_fare_sgd is null, so POL-RD-11 - which would close off the distance refund as one the rider never lost - does not apply. If the deviation stands, the remedy is POL-RD-02 arithmetic and not discretion: charged_total 21.32 less a recomputed fare of 13.32 (base 3.80 + 0.75 x 6.4 km + 0.28 x 14.0 min, surge multiplier 1.0 read from the fare breakdown, plus the 0.80 platform fee), giving a refund of 8.00. That is above the 0.50 de minimis floor and short of the 90% full-refund share, so it is a PARTIAL_REFUND of 8.00, not the 12.00 the rider asked for and not a FULL_REFUND.

The rider's establishment rests on unimpaired evidence. The trace carries 207 fixes at a 10-second interval with 100% coverage, no gaps and a maximum gap of 0 seconds, so limbs (a) to (c) of POL-RD-07 do not fire, no independent corroboration is required of the rider, and neither POL-RD-10(3) nor the POL-GEN-02 confidence cap is engaged. Every artifact the rider relies on carries weight 1.0.

The rider's own claim history does not raise the bar she must clear: rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 1, well below the 4-claim trigger in POL-RD-08, so the additional-corroboration requirement for low-value excess does not apply to a claim that is otherwise proven. Under POL-GEN-01 the remaining fields on the rider profile - rating, account age, lifetime trips, prior disputes - are context only and cannot be used to discount her account of this trip.

The rider does not overreach for the POL-RD-06 uplift, and says so on the record: the driver's trailing-90-day figures are deviation_flags_90d 0 over completed_trips_90d 511, so no repeat pattern is established, no full-refund uplift follows from it and no conduct referral is sought. The rider's monetary remedy is the POL-RD-02 partial - the arithmetic figure of 8.00 - and nothing more.

claims.text: The rider asked for this detour herself. MSG-00109-001 in the chat log was sent by RIDER at 18:22:06, roughly a minute after the meter started at 18:21:10, and reads 'hi can stop at jurong point first? need to grab something 5 min'; the platform resolved that message to a waypoint_hint of Jurong Point PHV Pickup Point, 1 Jurong West Central 2 (VEN-JURONG-POINT). That satisfies every limb of POL-RD-04: the instruction comes from the rider, it is timestamped before the vehicle left the optimal corridor rather than more than three minutes after, and it names a place specifically enough to act on. The driver accepted it thirteen seconds later with 'ok can, i wait at the phv pickup point'.

The trace corroborates the requested stop, so POL-RD-04's corroboration test is run and passed rather than undecidable. EV-GPS-00109 is unbroken 10-second telemetry with 100% coverage, 207 fixes and max_gap_sec of 0.0, and its admissibility assessment records the vehicle stationary 38 m from the Jurong Point PHV pickup point named in the rider's own message for 366 seconds, well inside the 200 m corroboration radius the clause requires. The same trace lists a 0.0 km/h speed sample among its distinct speeds, which is a vehicle waiting at a pickup point, not a vehicle driving past one.

Because the detour was rider-caused, the excess distance between leaving and rejoining the optimal corridor is excluded before POL-RD-01 and POL-RD-02 are applied, as POL-RD-04 expressly directs. The derived deviation block measures 7.36 km of excess at 115.00% of an optimal of 6.4 km, but that block is itself computed on the raw trace total (trace_distance_km 13.76 against optimal_distance_km 6.4) and takes no account of the exclusion the clause requires. Once the rider-requested Jurong Point leg is removed, the deviation gate in POL-RD-01 is not met and no POL-RD-02 recomputation runs.

No residual excess above the POL-RD-01 threshold is shown on this record. The 7.36 km and 115.00% figures are unadjusted totals; nothing in the derived block, the trip record or the fare breakdown isolates a post-exclusion excess, and under POL-RD-08 the rider carries the burden of proving an excess measured after the rider-caused leg comes out. A materiality figure computed before the adjustment the governing clause mandates cannot discharge that burden.

The POL-RD-06 profile check comes back clean and no uplift or referral is available on it. Even if the judge treats a material deviation as recorded, driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against driver_profile.completed_trips_90d of 511, a ratio of 0.00, far below the 0.05 with at least 40 completed trips that POL-RD-06 requires before a pattern is established. No pattern means no limb (a) tilt of a balanced record, no limb (b) uplift of the contested SGD 21.32 to a FULL_REFUND, and no limb (c) conduct referral. The lifetime counter prior_deviation_flags is not the trailing-90-day field the clause names and cannot be substituted for it.

The driver is owed compensation for distance the platform never billed. fare_breakdown.distance_charged_km is 9.60 while the governing gps_trace.trace_distance_km is 13.76, a shortfall of 4.16 km that exceeds the 1.0 km gate in POL-RD-04's compensation limb. At SGD 0.75 per unbilled kilometre that is 3.12, rounded up to the nearest SGD 0.05 as SGD 3.15, comfortably inside the SGD 15.00 per-trip cap. The payments artifact flags the shortfall itself as a substantive POL-RD-04 finding, not a cross-source data error.

No traffic advisory exists for this trip and the driver does not need one: EV-ADVIS-00109-01 is MISSING from the pool, carries no payload, and has admissibility weight 0.0 with issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, so no POL-RD-03 closure exoneration is asserted or available. The absence is citable and it is the platform's own assessment that 'the detour is explained by the rider's own instruction, not by any road condition' — which is precisely the POL-RD-04 route the driver relies on.

There is no pass-through money to correct on top. The fare breakdown carries no ERP gantries and erp_lines total 0.00, no tolls, an airport surcharge of 0.00 on a trip that neither originates nor ends at an airport, no promo discount and no waiting-time fee, so POL-RD-09 gives the rider nothing to add to the contested amount. The only contested money is the distance and time charge on the trip the rider herself asked to be extended.

On the rider's claim the present state stands, and the outcome this case produces is compensation to the driver. fare_breakdown.payment_status is CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd is 0.00; with POL-RD-04 exonerating the detour there is no POL-RD-02 recomputation to displace that charge, and under POL-GEN-03 NO_ACTION on a rider-filed dispute leaves the charge exactly as it is rather than restoring or increasing it. The ruling should therefore be DRIVER_COMPENSATION of SGD 3.15, with amount_sgd carrying that same figure, no refund to the rider, and no referral, since POL-RD-06(c) is not triggered.

ruling.explanation:
This ruling turns on who caused the extra distance, and the record answers that plainly.

To the rider: your own chat message MSG-00109-001, sent at 18:22:06 — about a minute after the meter started at 18:21:10 — asked the driver to 'stop at jurong point first'. The platform resolved that message to the Jurong Point PHV Pickup Point on the waypoint_hint field, and the GPS trace (EV-GPS-00109: 207 fixes, 10-second interval, 100% coverage, no gaps) shows the vehicle stationary 38 m from that point for 366 seconds, well inside the 200 m corroboration radius. That brings the whole detour within POL-RD-04: the driver accepted the instruction, it was given before the vehicle left the optimal corridor, and it named a place specifically enough to act on. The excess distance between leaving and rejoining the optimal corridor is therefore excluded before POL-RD-01 is applied. The trace is complete and shows the only off-corridor excursion was your requested stop, so the excluded stretch accounts for the entire measured excess: the 13.76 km driven reduces to the booked 6.4 km optimal, no excess remains, and no route-deviation refund is payable. Your 7.36 km / 115% figure is the unadjusted total — it is the pre-exclusion arithmetic, and it does not survive the exclusion the governing clause requires. Your remaining points are accepted: the trace is unimpaired, no traffic advisory exists for this corridor (EV-ADVIS-00109-01 is MISSING at weight 0.0, and its absence is citable but carries no fact), POL-RD-05 and POL-RD-12 do not apply, and POL-RD-06 yields no uplift or referral.

To the driver: your detour is excused, and separately the fare record shows you were under-billed. EV-FARE-00109 records distance_charged_km of 9.60 against the governing gps_trace.trace_distance_km of 13.76 — a shortfall of 4.16 km, above the 1.0 km gate in POL-RD-04's compensation limb. At SGD 0.75 per unbilled kilometre that is SGD 3.12, rounded up to the nearest SGD 0.05 as SGD 3.15, comfortably inside the SGD 15.00 per-trip cap. That is the money this ruling moves: SGD 3.15 is carried in both amount_sgd and driver_compensation_sgd, the rider's charge of SGD 21.32 stands and is not refunded, and no referral is recorded. POL-RD-06 is clean (deviation_flags_90d 0 against completed_trips_90d 511, no repeat pattern), so no conduct referral, and there is no phantom gantry or misapplied surcharge to refer under POL-RD-09(4). Every artifact carrying a deciding fact — EV-CHAT-00109, EV-GPS-00109 and EV-FARE-00109 — is at weight 1.0, and the profile fields mentioned on both sides are context-only.

Both parties: the trip did run long, but the record shows the rider asked for the detour, so the fare stands and the driver is owed a small platform payment for the distance the meter never charged.

To the rider: on the governing GPS trace (EV-GPS-00109, 13.76 km) against the booked optimal of 6.4 km, the excess is real — but it is the detour you requested. Your own in-app message at 18:22:06, about a minute into the trip, read 'can stop at jurong point first? need to grab something 5 min', and the platform resolved it to the Jurong Point PHV pickup point. The driver accepted 25 seconds later, and the unbroken trace puts the car stationary 38 m from that point for 366 seconds — inside the 200 m radius POL-RD-04 requires, so the clause's corroboration test is run and passed, not left undecidable. Under POL-RD-04 the excess between leaving and rejoining the optimal corridor is excluded BEFORE POL-RD-01 and POL-RD-02 are applied. Here the car left the optimal corridor at the start to run to Jurong Point and rejoined it only at Bukit Batok, so the whole 7.36 km excess is attributable to your instruction. Nothing is left over: no deviation is established under POL-RD-01 and no POL-RD-02 recomputation is due. I have considered the argument that the record contains no derived figure isolating the post-exclusion excess, and that POL-RD-04 excuses the detour only 'to the extent' attributable. With the corridor exit and rejoin falling at the trip's endpoints, there is no residual excess to refund; the derived 7.36 km / 115% block is the unadjusted pre-exclusion measurement the governing clause directs me to adjust. Your claim that the driver 'anyhow drove' is not borne out, and the SGD 21.32 charge stands (payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd 0.00). For transparency the line items are: charged total SGD 21.32; a recomputed fare under POL-RD-02 would be SGD 13.32 and the difference SGD 8.00, but POL-RD-02 does not run because no deviation survives the POL-RD-04 exclusion.

To the driver: separately, the fare breakdown (EV-FARE-00109) bills 9.6 km while the trace records 13.76 km driven — a 4.16 km shortfall, above the 1.0 km gate in POL-RD-04's compensation limb. You are granted SGD 3.15 (4.16 km x SGD 0.75 = SGD 3.12, rounded UP to the nearest SGD 0.05, within the SGD 15.00 cap). That is a platform-funded payment; it is not netted against the rider's fare and the rider's own charge is unchanged.

On the artifacts: EV-GPS-00109 is unimpaired for policy purposes (207 fixes, 10 s interval, 100% coverage, no gaps, maximum gap 0.0 s), so POL-RD-07 does not fire and no independent corroboration is demanded of either side. EV-ADVIS-00109-01 (traffic advisory) is absent from the pool at weight 0.0 with issue MISSING_ARTIFACT; no road-condition exoneration under POL-RD-03 is claimed or available, and nothing in this ruling rests on it. There are no ERP, toll or airport-surcharge lines, so POL-RD-09 corrects nothing and produces no billing-integrity referral. The driver's 90-day record (0 deviation flags over 511 completed trips) establishes no repeat pattern, so POL-RD-06 gives no full-refund uplift and no conduct referral; the rider's claim history (1 claim in 60 days) does not trigger the extra-corroboration rule in POL-RD-08. Profile fields are credibility weighting only under POL-GEN-01 and decide nothing here. No POL-RD-10 escalation trigger fires: confidence is above the 0.70 floor, the trip identifiers match, the trace is unimpaired and corroborated, and no charge line lacks a counterpart. Ruling: DRIVER_COMPENSATION of SGD 3.15.

ruling.explanation:
To the rider and the driver: the rider's charge stands, no refund is due to her, and the driver is owed SGD 3.15 for distance the platform did not bill.

WHY THERE IS NO RIDER REFUND. The deviation is measured on the GPS trace, as POL-RD-01 requires: 13.76 km driven against a booked optimal of 6.4 km, an excess of 7.36 km (115%). That clears both gates (over 0.8 km and over 20%) and is additionally a MATERIAL deviation. But it is fully excused under POL-RD-04 because the rider asked for it. Her own message, sent at 18:22:06 — about a minute after the meter started — reads 'hi can stop at jurong point first? need to grab something 5 min', and the platform resolved it to the Jurong Point PHV pickup point (VEN-JURONG-POINT). That is exactly the kind of specific, rider-sent instruction the clause names. The 10-second trace is continuous (207 fixes, 100% coverage, maximum gap 0 s) and records the vehicle stationary 38 m from that waypoint for 366 seconds — well inside the 200 m corroboration radius. The whole of the 7.36 km excess is the distance of that rider-requested Jurong Point leg, so the clause excludes it before POL-RD-01 is applied. No residual excess clears the threshold, no deviation stands, and POL-RD-02 never runs; the SGD 12.00 the rider asked for is not payable. I do not accept the rider's argument that the excused portion is unmeasured: the trace is the measurement, it is unimpaired, and it shows the only departure from the optimal corridor is the one the rider herself requested.

WHY THE DRIVER IS PAID. The fare breakdown bills 9.60 km while the governing trace records 13.76 km. That 4.16 km shortfall exceeds the 1.0 km gate in POL-RD-04, so the driver is granted SGD 0.75 per unbilled kilometre: 4.16 x 0.75 = 3.12, rounded up to SGD 3.15 and inside the SGD 15.00 cap. This is a platform-funded payment; it does not increase or restore any charge against the rider.

POINTS DEALT WITH IN PASSING. The traffic-advisory artifact is MISSING, carries weight 0.0 and fired MISSING_ARTIFACT; both sides disclosed this. It exonerates nothing under POL-RD-03 and no finding rests on it. The trace is not impaired under POL-RD-07(a)-(c), so no independent corroboration was required of the rider and no POL-RD-10(3) escalation arises. The driver's trailing-90-day record — 0 deviation flags over 511 completed trips — establishes no repeat pattern, so POL-RD-06 gives no full-refund uplift and no conduct referral. Profile fields other than the counters the clauses actually name (rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d; driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d and completed_trips_90d) are context only and were not used against either party. No POL-RD-10 escalation trigger fires, so this ruling is final.

Confidence 0.90, capped at 1.0 by the weight-1.0 artifacts that carry the deciding facts (chat log, GPS trace and fare breakdown).

Under POL-GEN-01 the remaining fields on the rider profile - rating, account age, lifetime trips, prior disputes - are context only and cannot be used to discount her account of this trip.

ledger.claim: Threshold matter for the record: the three artifacts describe the same trip. The trip_id TRP-00109 appears on the trip record, the GPS trace and the fare breakdown, and the trace's first fix (2026-07-21T18:21:10) matches the trip record's started_at to the second, so the rider's initial burden under limb (a) is discharged on matching identifiers and a matching pickup timestamp.

On the governing trace field the trip covers 13.76 km against a booked optimal of 6.4 km - an excess of 7.36 km, which is 115% of the optimal route. Both POL-RD-01 gates are cleared (more than 0.8 km absolute, more than 20% relative), and because the excess also exceeds 50% of optimal the deviation is additionally MATERIAL, exactly as the trace-derived status records. The rider's limb (b) burden is discharged.

POL-RD-01 makes gps_trace.trace_distance_km the governing measurement and expressly forbids citing trip_record.actual_distance_km for the threshold test. The rider measures on the trace's 13.76 km, and that figure clears the gate by itself, so nothing in this case turns on the rounded 13.8 km convenience copy on the trip record.

The traffic-advisory artifact is MISSING: no advisory covers this corridor on this trip, and absence is citable. I disclose that EV-ADVIS-00109-01 carries weight 0.0, has no payload, and fired the issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT. With no named road or expressway segment, no validity window overlapping the trace, and no matched corridor exit and rejoin, POL-RD-03 exonerates nothing here - the driver has no road-condition answer to the deviation.

Neither of the other baseline-lifting clauses is available to the driver. pickup_amended_at and dropoff_amended_at are both null and amended_optimal_distance_km is null, so there is no re-quote for POL-RD-05 to re-run POL-RD-01 against; and vehicle_type is RYDE_X, not RYDE_POOL, so the matched-itinerary baseline of POL-RD-12 never arises. The comparison stays where the rider put it: 13.76 km driven against 6.4 km optimal.

The rider's own message at 18:22:06 asked for a stop - 'stop at jurong point first? need to grab something 5 min'. POL-RD-04 excuses a deviation only 'to the extent' it is attributable to such an instruction: it excludes the excess distance between leaving and rejoining the optimal corridor and nothing beyond that. It does not reclassify the whole 7.36 km excess as a lawful trip, it does not displace POL-RD-01 or POL-RD-02 for any excess left over from the subtraction, and the size of the attributable portion is the driver's to establish under POL-RD-08. The record carries no derived measurement of that portion at all, so the exclusion cannot be shown to consume the rider's whole excess.

The fare model is METERED and quoted_fare_sgd is null, so POL-RD-11 - which would close off the distance refund as one the rider never lost - does not apply. If the deviation stands, the remedy is POL-RD-02 arithmetic and not discretion: charged_total 21.32 less a recomputed fare of 13.32 (base 3.80 + 0.75 x 6.4 km + 0.28 x 14.0 min, surge multiplier 1.0 read from the fare breakdown, plus the 0.80 platform fee), giving a refund of 8.00. That is above the 0.50 de minimis floor and short of the 90% full-refund share, so it is a PARTIAL_REFUND of 8.00, not the 12.00 the rider asked for and not a FULL_REFUND.

The rider's establishment rests on unimpaired evidence. The trace carries 207 fixes at a 10-second interval with 100% coverage, no gaps and a maximum gap of 0 seconds, so limbs (a) to (c) of POL-RD-07 do not fire, no independent corroboration is required of the rider, and neither POL-RD-10(3) nor the POL-GEN-02 confidence cap is engaged. Every artifact the rider relies on carries weight 1.0.

The rider's own claim history does not raise the bar she must clear: rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 1, well below the 4-claim trigger in POL-RD-08, so the additional-corroboration requirement for low-value excess does not apply to a claim that is otherwise proven. Under POL-GEN-01 the remaining fields on the rider profile - rating, account age, lifetime trips, prior disputes - are context only and cannot be used to discount her account of this trip.

ledger.claim: The rider does not overreach for the POL-RD-06 uplift, and says so on the record: the driver's trailing-90-day figures are deviation_flags_90d 0 over completed_trips_90d 511, so no repeat pattern is established, no full-refund uplift follows from it and no conduct referral is sought. The rider's monetary remedy is the POL-RD-02 partial - the arithmetic figure of 8.00 - and nothing more.

The rider asked for this detour herself. MSG-00109-001 in the chat log was sent by RIDER at 18:22:06, roughly a minute after the meter started at 18:21:10, and reads 'hi can stop at jurong point first? need to grab something 5 min'; the platform resolved that message to a waypoint_hint of Jurong Point PHV Pickup Point, 1 Jurong West Central 2 (VEN-JURONG-POINT). That satisfies every limb of POL-RD-04: the instruction comes from the rider, it is timestamped before the vehicle left the optimal corridor rather than more than three minutes after, and it names a place specifically enough to act on. The driver accepted it thirteen seconds later with 'ok can, i wait at the phv pickup point'.

The trace corroborates the requested stop, so POL-RD-04's corroboration test is run and passed rather than undecidable. EV-GPS-00109 is unbroken 10-second telemetry with 100% coverage, 207 fixes and max_gap_sec of 0.0, and its admissibility assessment records the vehicle stationary 38 m from the Jurong Point PHV pickup point named in the rider's own message for 366 seconds, well inside the 200 m corroboration radius the clause requires. The same trace lists a 0.0 km/h speed sample among its distinct speeds, which is a vehicle waiting at a pickup point, not a vehicle driving past one.

Because the detour was rider-caused, the excess distance between leaving and rejoining the optimal corridor is excluded before POL-RD-01 and POL-RD-02 are applied, as POL-RD-04 expressly directs. The derived deviation block measures 7.36 km of excess at 115.00% of an optimal of 6.4 km, but that block is itself computed on the raw trace total (trace_distance_km 13.76 against optimal_distance_km 6.4) and takes no account of the exclusion the clause requires. Once the rider-requested Jurong Point leg is removed, the deviation gate in POL-RD-01 is not met and no POL-RD-02 recomputation runs.

No residual excess above the POL-RD-01 threshold is shown on this record. The 7.36 km and 115.00% figures are unadjusted totals; nothing in the derived block, the trip record or the fare breakdown isolates a post-exclusion excess, and under POL-RD-08 the rider carries the burden of proving an excess measured after the rider-caused leg comes out. A materiality figure computed before the adjustment the governing clause mandates cannot discharge that burden.

The POL-RD-06 profile check comes back clean and no uplift or referral is available on it. Even if the judge treats a material deviation as recorded, driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against driver_profile.completed_trips_90d of 511, a ratio of 0.00, far below the 0.05 with at least 40 completed trips that POL-RD-06 requires before a pattern is established. No pattern means no limb (a) tilt of a balanced record, no limb (b) uplift of the contested SGD 21.32 to a FULL_REFUND, and no limb (c) conduct referral. The lifetime counter prior_deviation_flags is not the trailing-90-day field the clause names and cannot be substituted for it.

ledger.claim: The driver is owed compensation for distance the platform never billed. fare_breakdown.distance_charged_km is 9.60 while the governing gps_trace.trace_distance_km is 13.76, a shortfall of 4.16 km that exceeds the 1.0 km gate in POL-RD-04's compensation limb. At SGD 0.75 per unbilled kilometre that is 3.12, rounded up to the nearest SGD 0.05 as SGD 3.15, comfortably inside the SGD 15.00 per-trip cap. The payments artifact flags the shortfall itself as a substantive POL-RD-04 finding, not a cross-source data error.

No traffic advisory exists for this trip and the driver does not need one: EV-ADVIS-00109-01 is MISSING from the pool, carries no payload, and has admissibility weight 0.0 with issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, so no POL-RD-03 closure exoneration is asserted or available. The absence is citable and it is the platform's own assessment that 'the detour is explained by the rider's own instruction, not by any road condition' — which is precisely the POL-RD-04 route the driver relies on.

There is no pass-through money to correct on top. The fare breakdown carries no ERP gantries and erp_lines total 0.00, no tolls, an airport surcharge of 0.00 on a trip that neither originates nor ends at an airport, no promo discount and no waiting-time fee, so POL-RD-09 gives the rider nothing to add to the contested amount. The only contested money is the distance and time charge on the trip the rider herself asked to be extended.

On the rider's claim the present state stands, and the outcome this case produces is compensation to the driver. fare_breakdown.payment_status is CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd is 0.00; with POL-RD-04 exonerating the detour there is no POL-RD-02 recomputation to displace that charge, and under POL-GEN-03 NO_ACTION on a rider-filed dispute leaves the charge exactly as it is rather than restoring or increasing it. The ruling should therefore be DRIVER_COMPENSATION of SGD 3.15, with amount_sgd carrying that same figure, no refund to the rider, and no referral, since POL-RD-06(c) is not triggered.
